Subject: Service provider classification and telemetry subprocessors — initial ask

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. As part of HealthyLabs' assessment for a pilot, our legal team wants a concise write-up of how Redwood treats telemetry/operational logs and whether you consider Redwood a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA for the telemetry data we would send during inference. Specific asks: 

- Confirm whether Redwood will be acting as a service provider (limited use) versus a controller/processor role for operational telemetry and aggregated analytics.
- List current subprocessors that process telemetry (including cloud regions they operate in). We need onshore fallback options for telemetry in case of regulatory restrictions.
- Provide a draft clause we can propose to our contracting team that restricts offshore subprocessors for telemetry and defines retention limits.

We have a targeted timeline to finish legal review by May 7 so any early docs are appreciated.

Appreciate it,
Amir

Amir,

Thanks for the clear asks — helpful. High level answers up front, with attachments and recommended clause below. Full details attached (dataflow matrix + draft US addendum).

Summary:
- Redwood treats customer inference inputs and associated invocation metadata as "service provider" data under CCPA/CPRA when we are processing on behalf of a customer and are bound by contractual limited-use restrictions. That classification applies to telemetry that is operational-only (latency, error rates, per-route usage) so long as the telemetry does not include customer PII that the customer has not authorized us to process.
- We maintain a list of subprocessors; for telemetry we primarily use our metrics pipeline (internal) and managed cloud monitoring services. The current subprocessors that may touch telemetry are listed in the attached dataflow matrix.
- Onshore fallback: we can lock telemetry processing to US regions (and in many cases to a customer-dedicated Dedicated cluster) to meet onshore-only requirements. There is an operational change window (2–4 weeks) and a small delta in per-token cost for dedicated telemetry lanes.

Suggested contract language (for your counsel):
"Redwood will process operational telemetry and aggregated analytics as a Service Provider under applicable US privacy laws. For telemetry originating from Customer accounts where Customer has designated 'onshore-only' processing, Redwood will ensure that telemetry is processed and stored solely in the United States. Redwood will not engage offshore subprocessors to process such telemetry unless Redwood has obtained Customer's prior written consent or unless required by law. Retention of telemetry used for operational debugging and analytics will not exceed 90 days unless Customer requests otherwise in writing.
"Redwood will provide, upon reasonable request and subject to appropriate confidentiality protections, an up-to-date list of subprocessors and their processing locations."

Attachments sent: redwood-us-privacy-addendum-draft.docx, redwood-dataflow-matrix.csv, onshore-fallback-diagram.pdf

Amir / Greenshore procurement team,

Following up with the materials and a compact answers bundle for your counsel and procurement. See attachments (same as before), and below a short FAQ that we find helpful for legal reviewers.

FAQ — short answers for counsel:
Q: Will Redwood act as a Service Provider for telemetry?
A: Yes — when telemetry is operational-only and processed strictly on behalf of the customer under contractual limited-use terms, Redwood will accept Service Provider classification for US privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA).

Q: What about telemetry that inadvertently contains customer PII?
A: If telemetry contains PII that the Customer has not authorized Redwood to process, we will treat that as data outside the limited-use scope and will coordinate with Customer to remediate (delete or return) per the DPA. The addendum includes a required notification and remediation timeline (48 hours for suspected accidental PII exposure).

Q: Can you provide an onshore-only guarantee?
A: Yes. We offer an onshore-only telemetry option (US regions + Dedicated telemetry lane). Contractually we can restrict offshore subprocessors for that telemetry and include a notice/fall-back clause. There is a standard charge for dedicated telemetry lanes; exact pricing is in the SOW.

Q: Subprocessor visibility?
A: We will provide an up-to-date subprocessors list and an annual notice for changes; for high-risk telemetry we can agree to pre-approval of any new subprocessor that would process onshore-only telemetry.
